How to apply?
In the following sections, you will find all the information you need to apply to the graduate programs in Biological Sciences at the University of Delaware. For an overview of the general admission requirements, please view the Overview of Admission Requirements. The specific requirements for each program can be found in the Application details for each degree program. Finally, the Application FAQs have useful information on our programs and the application process.
Admission Requirements
Application Details
Application FAQs
Requirements for Admission (MS, PhD)
Admission criteria for the Department of Biological Sciences thesis-based MS and PhD programs include a minimum scholastic index (grade point average on a 4.0 scale) of 2.8 overall and 3.0 in the sciences. Applicants are required to have completed the following coursework, or its equivalent: two years of biological sciences; one year of mathematics, preferably including calculus and/or statistics; one year of college physics; one year of general chemistry; and one course in organic chemistry. Applicants who did not major in biology may still be considered if they have completed two years of biological sciences coursework and have a strong academic background in other scientific disciplines.
Requirements for Admission (non-thesis MS)
Applicants to the non-thesis MS program must hold a Bachelor's degree (BA or BS) before matriculation. Applicants should have completed at least two years of biological sciences coursework, one semester of mathematics (preferably calculus and/or statistics), one year each of college physics and inorganic chemistry, and one course in organic chemistry. A minimum GPA of 3.0, both cumulative and science-specific, is recommended.
Requirements for Admission (4+1 programs)
The Biological Sciences BS/Biology MS 4+1 and Biological Sciences BA/Biology MS 4+1 programs are available only to University of Delaware students majoring in Biological Sciences. Applicants must be in their junior year and enrolled full time at the time of application. A minimum GPA of 3.0 both in the major and overall is recommended. Applicants are expected to have completed at least two years of biological sciences coursework, one semester of mathematics, one year each of college physics and inorganic chemistry, and one course in organic chemistry. Students must also have completed at least one course at or above the 400 level in the undergraduate major.
Foreign National Applicants
International applicants must earn a score of at least 100 on the Test of English as a Foreign Language (TOEFL) or at least 7.5 on the International English Language Testing System (IELTS), in accordance with University of Delaware requirements for graduate assistantship eligibility. Previous education, training, or residence in the U.S. does not automatically exempt foreign nationals from these requirements. Requests to waive the language testing requirement - for example, for students from English-speaking countries outside the U.S. or for foreign students who earned a college degree from a U.S. institution - must be approved by the University of Delaware Graduate College.
Admission to the graduate programs is competitive. Meeting the stated requirements does not guarantee admission, and applicants who do not meet every requirement may still be considered if they demonstrate other appropriate strengths.
Requirements for Application (MS, PhD)
Applications must include three letters of recommendation from individuals able to assess the applicant's potential for graduate study, an undergraduate transcript, a resume or CV describing academic and/or work experience, and a personal statement. The GRE is neither required nor considered. The personal statement should address the following questions:
What scientific research experience have you had?
What are your research interests and long-term professional objectives?
What specific attributes of our Department make you feel that it would be a good place for you?
If applicable, are there any special circumstances related to your academic record that you feel we should know about?
Applications are considered only for fall entrance. For optimal consideration for Fall admission, all application materials should be submitted by December 15th, although applications will be considered until April 15th if there are remaining positions in the program. Foreign nationals are encouraged to apply by the full consideration deadlines to give sufficient time to obtain the necessary visas for graduate study in the USA.
Requirements for Application (non-thesis MS)
Applications must include three letters of recommendation from individuals able to assess the applicant's potential for graduate study, an undergraduate transcript, a resume or CV describing academic and/or work experience, and a personal statement. The GRE is neither required nor considered. For optimal consideration for fall admission to the non-thesis MS program, all application materials should be completed by January 15. Applications may continue to be considered through July 1 if positions remain available. Foreign nationals are encouraged to apply by the January 15 deadline to allow sufficient time to obtain the visas required for graduate study in the United States.
Requirements for Application (4+1 programs)
Applications to the 4+1 program must include an unofficial University of Delaware transcript and two letters of recommendation. At least one recommendation must be provided by a faculty member in the Department of Biological Sciences. The GRE is neither required nor considered. Applications to the 4+1 program are reviewed by the Department of Biological Sciences Graduate Affairs Committee beginning January 15 and are considered on a rolling basis until all available positions are filled.
How do I apply? Electronic application must be made through the University of Delaware's Office of Graduate & Professional Education.
Must I have prior research experience to be admitted? Over 95% of students admitted to the thesis-based MS and Ph.D. applicants have prior, substantive research experience. This must be well documented in the application.
What if I don’t know which laboratory in which to conduct my research? PhD students are not admitted directly into research mentor laboratories. MS students must chose their research mentor at the beginning of their first semester in the program. Ph.D. students perform 2-3 laboratory rotations during the first year in the program and choose their mentor from these rotation experiences.
When is the application deadline? Our priority deadline is December 15th of each academic year. Applications that come in after this deadline will be considered if additional space is available. Applications for international students will not be considered if received after April 1st and domestic applicants will not be considered if received after April 15th.
How large is the Biological Sciences graduate program? As of fall 2026, there are over 75students enrolled in our thesis-based MS & PhD graduate programs, all of which receive tuition scholarships and a stipend.
Are GREs required? The Department is waiving the GRE requirement for our graduate program. You do not need to take or share a GRE score to apply.
How long will it likely take me to complete the PhD? The median time to degree for a typical PhD student is 5.5 years. Individual completion length varies by progress in coursework and research.
How are previous students employed after degree completion? Our previous graduates are employed in pharma industry, biotechnology, academic, and government sectors in a variety of positions such as Senior Scientist, Product manager, Faculty, and Medical writer positions.
